entities.name: Primary care surveillance improves trends
observations: A Castilla y León sentinel network covering 2.6% of the population produced weekly COVID-19/acute respiratory infection estimates described as correlating quite accurately with population-wide registration and detecting epidemic thresholds when standardized reporting and laboratory linkage were used.

entities.name: Primary-care surveillance undercounts
observations: Routine primary-care coding may capture diagnosed cases accurately but miss undiagnosed disease; Catalonia coeliac disease recorded prevalence was 1.99 per 1,000 versus estimated seroprevalence of 5 per 1,000, with code sensitivity 91.63%, specificity 99.95%, and PPV 63.85%.

entities.name: Primary-care estimates vary by disease
observations: Primary-care disease estimate validity depends on condition, database, and case definition; cancer registry comparisons found CPRD completeness of 65% (GOLD) and 77% (Aurum), while some validated incontinence definitions had sensitivity as low as 51.8%.

entities.name: Syndromic surveillance needs calibration
observations: Australian Flutracking symptom rates correlated with laboratory notifications among unvaccinated respondents but not vaccinated respondents, indicating that syndromic primary-care/community signals need adjustment before interpretation as confirmed influenza incidence.
